methodology: severed-wire-audit (PRODUCED minus CONSUMED), cross-referenced against review-results/config.md

findings.rationale: On serde_json::to_value(&schema) failure the function silently returns serde_json::Value::Object(Map::new()) == {} — an empty JSON Schema, which has zero constraints and therefore ACCEPTS EVERY instance (true schema). This is exactly the accept-all sentinel the sibling patcher path rejected: patcher.rs cached_config_schema() was fixed (config.md H2) to panic with 'type-system soundness failure'. The schema.rs fallback was left with a silent accept-all, so the two schema producers now diverge. Live consumer: config.schema RPC hands this Value to the Panel for client-side config-edit validation; a {} schema disables that validation silently. Server-side validation (ConfigPatcher + Config::validate) is unaffected, so blast radius is client-side only.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the unwrap_or_else fallback in generate_config_schema_json with the same panic used in patcher.rs cached_config_schema() (or a Result/expect), so the two schema producers share one policy: serialization failure is a type-soundness bug, not a recoverable error.
findings.risk: Low — can only trigger on a Config-type serialization bug, which already panics in the patcher path. Aligning to panic makes the failure loud instead of silently degrading the Panel's edit validation.
findings.verification: cargo test -p alephcore --lib schema; confirm generate_config_schema_json no longer contains an unwrap_or_else fallback; grep for Value::Object(Map::new()) in schema.rs returns nothing.
findings.existing_review_ref: config.md H2 (analogous site in patcher.rs already fixed to panic; schema.rs residual not covered)

findings.consumer_location: none found (only dead method ProfileConfig::is_tool_allowed at profile.rs:169 + tests in agent_env/mod.rs:1105,1127,1139)
findings.rationale: ProfileConfig docstring promises profiles define 'Tool whitelist (which tools are allowed)'. But the live tool gate is AgentInstanceConfig.tool_whitelist, which is sourced from agent.skills (agent_instance.rs:112 'tool_whitelist <- skills'), via tool_allowed_by (agent_instance.rs:631). ProfileConfig.tools is never bridged into that gate. Its only reader is ProfileConfig::is_tool_allowed (profile.rs:169) which has zero callers repo-wide, and its private glob_match (profile.rs:187). So [profiles.<name>].tools parses, serializes, and is discarded: an inert knob. Severed a long time with a newer mechanism (agent.skills / AgentDef.tool_whitelist) covering the outcome. Revive-vs-delete is a product call: is the profile's tool whitelist meant to gate workspaces, or is it superseded?
findings.proposed_change: If the profile whitelist is intended: bridge ProfileConfig.tools into AgentInstanceConfig.tool_whitelist at workspace/profile inheritance time (agent_env). If superseded: CUT the field, the dead is_tool_allowed/glob_match methods, and their tests; add a dead_keys entry for [profiles.*.tools].
findings.risk: Reconnecting adds real coupling between profile inheritance and the tool gate and may surprise existing deployments whose profiles declare tools but whose agents gate on skills. CUTting could break any external client that reads profiles.tools via config.get.
findings.verification: grep -rn 'profile.tools' and '.is_tool_allowed' to confirm zero live readers before cutting; or add a test asserting a workspace inheriting a profile with tools=[...] produces an AgentInstanceConfig whose tool_whitelist contains those patterns.

findings.rationale: The [policies.metrics] CONNECT from config.md (inert config bridged to live StageTimer) was done via init_metrics_runtime (src/metrics/mod.rs:62), but the bridge re-implemented the math instead of delegating: init_metrics_runtime duplicates the is_finite/>=0 guard and MetricsRuntime::warning_threshold_ms (src/metrics/mod.rs:84) duplicates the threshold computation, dropping the .clamp(0.0, f64::MAX) the config method performs. Net: MetricsPolicy::warning_threshold_ms has zero callers (dead), and two divergent copies of the threshold math now exist. The config method's field (warning_multiplier) IS consumed (init_metrics_runtime reads it), so only the METHOD is dead.
findings.proposed_change: Delete MetricsPolicy::warning_threshold_ms (and its #[test] test_warning_threshold). The live single source is MetricsRuntime::warning_threshold_ms; the guard already lives in init_metrics_runtime. Optionally fold the .clamp guard into MetricsRuntime::warning_threshold_ms so the non-finite edge can't produce a saturating u64::MAX threshold.
findings.risk: None if deleted — no caller. If instead CONNECTed by having init_metrics_runtime delegate, minor refactor risk in the metrics init path.
findings.verification: grep -rn 'MetricsPolicy' and '.warning_threshold_ms' confirm zero callers; cargo test -p alephcore --lib metrics after removal.
findings.existing_review_ref: config.md (policies.metrics CONNECT — this is the leftover dead method from that half-done bridge)
